title: U.S. House · Texas's 26th Congressional District
area: North Texas exurbs, including much of Denton County (Denton, Flower Mound, Lewisville).

context.text: Texas redrew its congressional district boundaries in August 2025 ahead of the 2026 elections, a mid-decade redistricting.

In the March 3, 2026 primaries, Brandon Gill defeated Robert Chick 91.1% to 8.9% for the Republican nomination, and Steven Shook defeated Ernest Lineberger III 51.1% to 48.9% for the Democratic nomination. Phil Gray advanced as the Libertarian Party's nominee from its March 21, 2026 convention.

positions.summary: His 2024 campaign website, as quoted by Ballotpedia, says he will not give an inch on gun control.
positions.quote: I will not give an inch on gun control.

positions.summary: His 2024 campaign website, as quoted by Ballotpedia, calls abortion something that needs to be abolished.
positions.quote: Abortion is an abomination that needs to be abolished.

positions.summary: His 2024 campaign website, as quoted by Ballotpedia, calls for reinstating "Remain in Mexico" and ending "Catch and Release".
positions.quote: Reinstate "Remain in Mexico" and end “Catch and Release”.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, the House Committee on the Judiciary, and the House Committee on the Budget in the 119th Congress.

candidates.name: Steven Shook
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary with 51.1% of the vote

priorities.text: In his Ballotpedia survey, listed his priorities as keeping rural hospitals open, lowering healthcare costs, supporting local businesses and job growth, strengthening public safety through community policing, and restoring accountability in Washington.

positions.summary: Campaign policy page calls for a step-by-step transition to universal healthcare.
positions.quote: Implement planned step-by step transition to universal healthcare.

positions.summary: Campaign policy page says he would close loopholes that allow gun sales without background checks and support red-flag laws.
positions.quote: Close loopholes that allow guns to be sold without background checks.

positions.summary: Campaign policy page says he opposes efforts to direct school funds to voucher programs.
positions.quote: oppose efforts to drain funds into unaccountable voucher programs

candidates.name: Phil Gray
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced as the Libertarian Party's nominee from its March 21, 2026 state convention

priorities.text: His campaign website centers on reducing the national debt, including a proposal to let immigrants pay to expedite entry with the funds used to pay down debt and fund low-interest loans in place of some tax-funded programs.

His campaign website (2024 version, as quoted by Ballotpedia) also lists decriminalizing drug use, reducing the cost of healthcare through price transparency, and returning most federal lands to the states.

statements.quote: I do not believe that it is the government’s place to decide this most painful of decisions. That decision is best left to the mother, and her doctor.
statements.context: On his campaign website, as quoted by Ballotpedia (2024 version)

statements.quote: For the undocumented, let them come out of the shadows, live and work freely. In exchange let them voluntary pay 10% of their earnings to our national debt fund.
statements.context: On his campaign website, as quoted by Ballotpedia (2024 version)

candidates.researchNotes: Campaign site text is taken from Ballotpedia's quotation of his 2024 website; his own sites (philgray.org, philgrayforcongress.org) did not load. 2026 wording was not verified. He has not completed a Candidate Connection survey.

researchNotes: Gill's positions are limited to official committee assignments; no 2026 Candidate Connection survey or campaign-site statements were found for him at research time. Shook completed his Candidate Connection survey in 2025, before the 2026 cycle. Phil Gray has not completed a 2026 Candidate Connection survey; his positions are drawn from his campaign website as reproduced by Ballotpedia. Federal key votes and FEC totals for the incumbent are added separately by script. Little biographical information on Phil Gray exists beyond his Ballotpedia profile (career, affiliations and election history); no personal background, education or news profile was found.
